slugs.format: @ + kebab-case, max 16 chars after the @, ASCII only (prefer english if you have to use greek, Greek is transliterated, e.g. θ→th, χ→ch)
slugs.collision_rule: if two headings would produce the same slug, append -2, -3, ... to the later ones
slugs.insertion_rule: ONLY inserted if the element doesn't already have an id — never overwrite an existing one

where_it_goes.h1:
on that slide's
Ενότητα N / M — ...
, NOT on the h1 itself — unless the slide has no eyebrow, or has one that doesn't contain the word 'Ενότητα' (title slide, closing cheatsheet/glossary slide), in which case it falls back to going directly on the h1
where_it_goes.h2_h3:
directly on the tag itself:

...

or

...

slugs.h2_h3_selection: not automatic/mechanical — only added in slides that are genuinely large, and only on pieces that are actually important (a named gotcha, a rule of thumb, an explicitly-flagged 'most important concept here' — not just any subheading). Roughly 1-4 slugs total per slide, spaced apart rather than clustered on adjacent headings.

how_to_generate.tool: extract_toc (Go, in the tocgen/ project — build with `go build -o extract_toc .`)

modes.0: eyebrows only — one slug per slide that has a qualifying 'Ενότητα' eyebrow, nothing else, no fallback
modes.1: h1 only (eyebrow-redirected where possible, direct-on-h1 fallback otherwise)

how_to_generate.note: the tool only ever inserts ids on h1/h2/h3 (mode-dependent) automatically — it does NOT pick 'important' h2/h3 for you; that selection is manual judgment, done by hand-editing specific headings' text to add id="@slug" before running the tool, or by picking them separately and inserting by hand

toc_entries.N: 1, 2, or 3 — matches the heading level, drives CSS indentation
toc_entries.text: the heading's own text, truncated to 45 characters (with … if cut)
toc_entries.no_data_slide: deliberately removed — navigation and everything else resolves via the href's id directly, never a stored slide number. Do not add one back.

toc_section_dividers.what: plain, non-clickable visual dividers grouping the <a> entries in the sidebar into sections — separate from and unrelated to slugs/navigation
toc_section_dividers.example:
ΕΙΣΑΓΩΓΗ
ΕΝΟΤΗΤΑ 1 — PACKAGES & PROJECT
ΕΝΟΤΗΤΑ 2 — CLI
toc_section_dividers.not_generated: extract_toc never produces these — no href, no @slug, not tied to any heading. Added by hand, interspersed among the <a> entries wherever a visual break between sections is wanted
toc_section_dividers.css_class: .toc-section (scoped under #toc-list), styled small-caps-ish: ~0.62rem, 600 weight, wide letter-spacing, dim color, a top border as the actual dividing line (removed on the first one via :first-child so the list doesn't open with a stray line)
toc_section_dividers.css_lives_in: style.css — not part of this project's tracked copy; added directly by the user in their own working file

where_toc_entries_go.location:
inside
...
, in the sidebar markup near the top of the HTML file (inside , before the deck)
where_toc_entries_go.action: paste the generated <a> tags (and any hand-placed toc-section dividers) directly inside that div, replacing whatever's currently there
where_toc_entries_go.order: should follow document order (top to bottom, matching the order headings appear in the file) — not required by the code, but keeps the sidebar sensible

click_behavior.mechanism: plain hash links — href="#@slug". Clicking fires the browser's native hashchange event, which script.js listens for globally and resolves via document.getElementById(hash) — no per-link JS needed, no click handlers, no data attributes
click_behavior.sidebar_highlighting: none — sidebar TOC entries are never highlighted or marked as 'active', on purpose. Do not reintroduce this.

safety.principle: every id insertion is a surgical text splice at an exact byte position — never a re-serialization through an HTML parser
safety.verification: strip every ` id="@..."` from the edited file and diff against the original — should be byte-identical
